question: to the Commission Juan Ignacio Zoido Álvarez (PPE), Carmen Crespo Díaz (PPE) Subject:

We recently learned about the text of the agreement on Gibraltar between the UK, Spain and the EU. This text does not resolve many of the main disputes in the relationship between Gibraltar and the neighbouring municipalities of Campo de Gibraltar, mainly those relating to taxation or the environment. For one thing, the agreement contains no measures concerning Gibraltar’s land reclamation activities in the Eastside project, which are having negative consequences on EU Special Areas of Conservation (SAC), fishing in the area and coastal conservation. Furthermore, the text fails to address how to protect the competitiveness of neighbouring EU ports, such as Algeciras, in the face of Gibraltar’s port, which allows bunkering and external anchorage in Gibraltarian waters. It also maintains the lack of reciprocity in the right of business establishment between Gibraltar and the EU, and the emissions trading scheme remains absent in Gibraltar, all while situations of unfair competition between ports in the area persist. In view of the above: 1.
Will the Commission allow Gibraltar to continue land reclamation activities on the EU’s SACs?
Has it assessed how the environmental and taxation differences maintained by the agreement will affect the competitiveness of neighbouring EU ports?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.7.2026) The future EU-UK Agreement in respect of Gibraltar agreement, once applied, will not affect the issue referred to by the Honourable Members. The future EU-UK Agreement in respect of Gibraltar contains solid Level Playing Field provisions regarding State aid, taxation, labour and social standards, environment, climate and sustainable development. These provisions are aimed at preventing distortions of competition affecting EU stakeholders, including EU ports. As regards taxation, environment, climate, social and labour standards, the Agreement provides for non-regression which ensures that parties cannot weaken or reduce the level of protection in the different areas below the level in place on 31 December 2020 affecting trade or investment. Specifically, as regards emissions trading, the Agreement (Article 220(2)) provides that the UK, in respect of Gibraltar, shall ensure that such system or measures shall have an equivalent scope and effectiveness as the one in place in the EU at the time of the entry into force of the Agreement.
